header:
Meeting: Model routing safety net synthesis
Date: 2026-01-17
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~75 min
Attendees: Sofia, Ethan, Maya, Leo (observer), Grace, Priya, Anil
Location: Zoom - internal
summary: Synthesis session to align on model routing safety nets for launch: define routing policies, fallback hierarchy, canary plan, rollback flows, and observability requirements. Focus on tradeoffs between latency, cost, and quality. Decided next steps and owners for policy matrix, canary, UI mock, and evals.
topics: Routing policy taxonomy (latency-first vs cost-first vs quality-fixed)
Fallback hierarchy: same-arch quantized -> smaller model -> burst to dedicated pool
Canary plan and metrics to capture (p50/p90/p99, token-per-second, cost delta, quality eval)
Console UX for emergency fallback and audit logs
Security/KMS and RBAC gating for forced fallbacks
Observability and traces needed for post-incident RCA
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: okay kickoff, thanks everyone for joining on a Saturday, I know it's a lot — um, quick agenda, routing policy matrix, canary plan, console UX, security checks.
[00:18] Ethan: yeah we got roughly 75 minutes, hope we can land owners. I'll start with a quick infra perspective — we saw last month the kv-cache pressure spike and routing jitter, so the safety net has to be both model and infra-aware.
[00:36] Maya: and from SE side customers keep asking for deterministic fallbacks, like, they want predictable latency rather than occasional high-cost hits. So we need clear heuristics.
[00:52] Grace: small note — quality regressions on quantized variants are often prompt-dependent, so we need a small eval suite in staging, otherwise ops will be chasing ghosts.
[01:08] Leo: (quiet) thanks team, just observing, will pass any blockers back to sales.
[01:18] Anil: can you define safety net again — is it only model fallbacks or also region/zone reroute?
[01:28] Sofia: good q; it's multi-tier: 1) same architecture quantized variant, 2) smaller model variant pinned for throughput, 3) route to dedicated/reserved pool if burst and customer tier allows, 4) degrade features (no streaming) as last resort.
[01:48] Ethan: re region fallback — we have policy-level routing today but automated region fallback needs network-aware decisions, TTL for cache invalidation, and compliance gating for some customers. We must ensure policy can be scoped per-account.
[02:06] Maya: on the UI, customers want an override toggle and an audit log entry — e.g., 'forced fallback on 01/17 by ops' and reason. Also SSO/SAML audit ties.
[02:22] Grace: KMS note — when we reroute to private deployment we need to ensure key access doesn't block tokenization. Edge case we hit before.
[02:40] Sofia: okay let's talk SLOs: target p99 generation latency 450ms for small-ol workloads, 1.2s for long-form. Fallback may add 10-40% latency but should preserve p90. Are we comfortable with that?
[02:58] Ethan: I think that's reasonable, but we need to define acceptable cost delta for fallback — we shouldn't spin up dedicated pool unless cost model is within commit thresholds. We'll capture cost delta metric.
[03:14] Maya: sales will push for low-latency guarantee, but we should present the safety net as explicit tradeoffs.
[03:24] Sofia: agreed, hence the routing policy matrix. It should map: intent (latency/cost/quality), primary model, fallback order, estimated cost delta, expected latency shift, and guardrails.
[03:42] Anil: what's the canary plan for this? We don't want a silent cascade.
[03:50] Ethan: propose a 48h staging canary with synthetic NRT traffic and 5% real traffic shadowing. Canary should exercise: prefix cache warmup, KV eviction, model variant switch, region fallback. We'll collect p50/p90/p99, token TPS, and rollback triggers if p99 exceeds threshold for X minutes.
[04:12] Grace: and add automated quality checks: sample outputs vs baseline and if a certain eval metric drops beyond delta, pause fallback. But that adds latency to decision loop.
[04:30] Maya: can we have manual override from console + automated escalation? typical flow: automated fallback -> notify oncall -> if oncall hits ack within 10m they can either roll forward or force rollback.
[04:48] Ethan: yes need integration with oncall and runbooks. Also instrumentation: trace must have model-variant labels, routing-reason tag, and audit id.
[05:04] Sofia: Grace, you mentioned KMS — if private routes are used, do we block fallback or is there a path?
[05:12] Grace: currently keys are per-customer and bound to region; for private deployments we'd require a key proxy or ephemeral delegation. That needs Security sign-off.
[05:26] Priya: from Product Ops — we need to capture cost attribution per customer for fallbacks, otherwise billing disputes happen. So every fallback event must log estimated token-cost delta.
[05:42] Ethan: agreed — telemetry must attach cost_estimate and route_reason. We'll need a pipeline to aggregate daily.
[06:00] Sofia: UX wireframes — Maya, do you have a quick sketch?
[06:06] Maya: yep, quick: top-level route policy tab, per-model fallback chain editable, emergency button in model-route row that shows active fallbacks and audit trail. Can push preview to sandbox.
[06:22] Leo: from AE perspective, we should script customer-facing language: "we'll maintain latency SLOs via controlled fallbacks; fallbacks may affect quality for certain prompts; customers can opt into strict quality mode."
[06:40] Grace: strict quality mode should disable automated fallbacks and instead route to dedicated pool only — that needs capacity reservation.
[06:50] Sofia: let's capture variants: name them clearly — e.g., baseline vX, quant-vX-q8, small-vX-1b. Avoid ambiguous naming.
[07:02] Anil: runbook question — if fallback triggers and then model-variant starts serving but causes hallucinations, what's the rollback criteria?
[07:14] Ethan: we'll require two signals: latency violation or quality regression flagged by eval -> and oncall confirmation if human-in-the-loop needed. Automatic rollback if p99 > threshold for 15m + cost spike.
[07:34] Grace: we should also add a guardrail that prevents fallback to models that were not in last successful deployment window; i.e., only approved model variants allowed.
[07:48] Sofia: security / compliance — RBAC: who can force fallbacks? Ops and SRE leads. And we log SSO ID and reason.
[08:00] Maya: small callout — console needs a read-only view for customers showing active fallback status and last fallback reason (no PII).
[08:12] Ethan: telemetry wise, we also need to correlate with kernel fallback events, OOMs, and scheduling delays. Otherwise it's hard to root cause.
[08:28] Grace: yeah last time we saw a kernel fallback correlate with a model routing jitter — traced back to driver upgrade. This time we need an RCA playbook mapping probable causes to remediation steps.
[08:44] Sofia: okay sketch of deliverables: routing policy matrix, canary job, UI mock, eval runs, security signoffs, and runbook. Owners next to each.
[08:58] Ethan: I'll own the canary job, and instrument telemetry.
[09:04] Maya: I'll do the UI mocks and link the audit log patterns.
[09:08] Grace: I'll run the quality evals and check KMS compatibility.
[09:12] Sofia: I'll produce the matrix and coordinate review. Priya will own cost attribution.
[09:18] Leo: sales wants a one-pager. We can produce customer-facing doc after internal signoff.
[09:24] Anil: on RCA playbook — I can draft probable cause tree and tie to runbook pages.
[09:30] Sofia: let's define canary success criteria now: p99 within 10% of baseline for 48h and no quality eval delta > 2% on critical prompts. If fail, rollback and manual review.
[09:48] Ethan: and a safety stop if cost delta > 30% for top 5 customers in sampling.
[09:56] Grace: question — do we allow fallback-induced partial responses? like streaming-disabled fallback? 
[10:06] Maya: we should, but show a clear flag in responses if streaming was turned off due to fallback. Customer-facing docs must explain this.
[10:18] Sofia: good point. Add to next steps: documentation of user-visible behavior.
[10:24] Priya: I'll coordinate with docs.
[10:28] Sofia: anything else?
[10:32] Ethan: one more technical nit — KV cache warming: when switching variants we lose cache affinity; we should try warmup prefetches for top prefixes. Canary should simulate prefix distribution.
[10:50] Grace: and log cache-miss rates per-variant.
[10:56] Sofia: perfect. Let's recap owners and due dates.
[11:04] Sofia: recap: Sofia - matrix by 1/22; Ethan - canary by 1/29; Maya - UI mock by 1/24; Grace - evals by 1/26; Anil - RCA playbook by 1/28; Priya - cost attribution pipeline by 1/29. All to review in sync next Friday.
[11:28] Leo: thanks team, I'll loop in sales ops for customer comms after the internal signoff.
[11:36] Sofia: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[11:42] (end)
